$comment: Three probes, same query, isolating whether the monotone climb is per pass or per byte of state.
It is per pass: many small chunks climb, few large chunks carrying the same total data do not.
Whether the residue is retained allocator arenas or redb's per-commit bookkeeping is NOT
established. It bounds how long a history a single catch-up can cross, and it is filed for C10.

$comment: THE GATE'S NUMBERS ARE THESE. C8 set the precedent and the reason has not changed: a developer
machine has no cgroup, so the local run declines to claim the gate and holds itself to a fixed
RSS budget instead. These come from the memo-ceiling job, which applies the ceiling with
systemd-run and sets CURRENT_CEILING_REQUIRED=1 so its absence would fail rather than pass.
CI run 31523102980, ubuntu-latest.
measured_in_ci.verdict: PASSED under a real 128 MiB ceiling: 384 MB of accumulated input streamed and 1.08 GB of state built, in a process whose resident memory peaked at 14.7 MB — 26:1 against the input and 73:1 against the state
measured_in_ci.what_the_two_platforms_say_about_the_per: 0.03% of the input on Linux against 0% to 3.1% on macOS. Both are small and both are positive; two orders of magnitude between them is evidence that the residue is the allocator's page-return policy rather than anything redb writes, which is the first real discrimination between the two candidates named above. It is still not proof, and C10 owns it.

the_page_cache_is_charged_to_the_cgroup.$comment: A memory cgroup charges the page cache, and dirty pages are not reclaimable until writeback has cleaned them. Writing a 384 MB fixture inside the ceiling therefore reaches memory.max and the OOM killer fires — timing-dependent, so it passed one CI run and failed the next with exit code 137, having printed only its own header.
the_page_cache_is_charged_to_the_cgroup.engine_involvement: none — the fixture had not finished being written when the process died
the_page_cache_is_charged_to_the_cgroup.fix: write_segment flushes and sync_data()s every epoch, bounding the dirty set at one epoch's frames (under a megabyte at this shape)
the_page_cache_is_charged_to_the_cgroup.cost: a few hundred fsyncs, fewer than the log itself performs for the same history
